PullRequest.Title: chat: add customization migration assessment telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Customization migration assessment telemetry with explicit lifecycle-owned reporting.

- keep computation and hint generation free of telemetry side effects
- expose an explicit `reportMigrationTelemetry(...)` method with aggregate-only payloads
- report completed assessments from the four intended lifecycle surfaces:
  - new chat in the editor
  - new-session composer in the Agents Window
  - existing session open
  - persisted session restore
- emit one event per non-empty migration category with only trigger, category, warning severity, and count
- remove informational severity until it has distinct product semantics
- add lifecycle-owner tests for all four reporting surfaces

Refs #332990

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint for changed files
- focused browser tests:
  - `ChatEditor` editor new-chat lifecycle
  - `NewChatWidget` Agents new-session lifecycle
  - `SessionsService` session-open lifecycle
  - `SessionsService` session-restore lifecycle
  - `CustomizationMigrationService` aggregate payload and telemetry-free compute/hint behavior
- changed files have no TypeScript diagnostics
- full type/layer checks remain locally blocked by unavailable Electron modules and the private Claude SDK package restore

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call chain from user chat navigation to the added line and from there to full migration/MCP computation is explicit. The only magnitude uncertainty is the user's number of configured prompts/MCP servers and tab-switch frequency.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Prompt discovery work and MCP configuration-resolution work for every known MCP server
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost repeats for every side-chat/subagent/tab open within the same session and grows with the number of prompt sources and configured MCP servers; sequential opens rebuild the MCP scope because the assessment disposes it when complete.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated background CPU/I/O pressure and avoidable telemetry/network traffic while navigating chats, which can make tab switching and the surrounding UI less responsive.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this line, `_openChat` only activated the selected chat and updated open telemetry; chat-tab navigation did not run customization migration discovery or MCP support assessment.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added fire-and-forget call invokes `reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` after every `_openChat`, including opens of side chats and subagent chats in a session that is already active.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 789 newly calls `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry(...)` inside `_openChat`, a method used for both entering a session and selecting another chat within the same session; no corresponding migration computation existed on this path before the PR.
Findings.Title: Report migration telemetry once per session open, not per chat tab
Findings.Impact: Opening or switching among chats in an already-open Agents session calls `_openChat` each time, so normal tab navigation repeatedly launches the complete customization assessment even though the session lifecycle has not changed.
Findings.Evidence: `openChat` always routes through `_openChatSession` to `_openChat`, and numerous chat-tab UI paths call it. The added line calls the helper unconditionally after load. That helper reaches `computeMigrations`, which runs all four migration computations; the MCP branch creates a ref-counted support scope, waits through its 50 ms delayed assessment, resolves every MCP server configuration, and disposes the scope afterward. Thus a later tab open recreates and reruns the assessment rather than reusing a completed result.
Findings.Recommendation: Move this report to the actual session-entry transition (or guard/deduplicate it by session resource for the current open lifecycle) and leave chat-only navigation free of migration recomputation.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Startup reachability, unbounded loop cardinality, detached concurrency, scope keying, and per-server work are all explicit in the code. Exact slowdown varies with restored-session and MCP-server counts, which affects severity rather than mechanism confidence.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent prompt discovery, per-workspace MCP support scopes, and per-server configuration-resolution work
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N immediately restored sessions with distinct workspace roots and M configured MCP servers, this loop starts N detached assessments at once and the MCP work grows as O(N×M); prompt listing is coalesced only when its cache is warm, while MCP scopes are keyed by session type and roots.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A burst of background CPU, filesystem/provider work, and asynchronous configuration resolution during workbench restore, increasing startup contention and responsiveness risk.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this loop was added, restoring the visible-session grid performed session resolution/layout only and did not launch customization discovery or MCP support assessments for each restored slot.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new loop fire-and-forgets one `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` call for every already-resolved restored session without a limiter, idle deferral, or grouping by equivalent assessment scope.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 1614 is inside a loop over all resolved restored sessions and newly starts one unawaited migration assessment per element; this startup fan-out did not exist before the PR.
Findings.Title: Bound migration assessments during session restore
Findings.Impact: Reloading an Agents window with several persisted visible sessions immediately launches a full customization assessment for every restored session just as the workbench is restoring. Different workspace roots prevent MCP-scope coalescing, so a realistic multi-session grid fans out concurrent work.
Findings.Evidence: `Workbench.restore` invokes `restoreVisibleSessions` during startup. At the added loop, every call synchronously enters `computeMigrations`; its MCP branch acquires a scope keyed by `[sessionType, roots]`. Each distinct scope schedules a 50 ms-delayed assessment, iterates all MCP servers, awaits local MCP loading, and resolves server configurations. The repository test itself demonstrates three calls for three restored sessions, and persisted visible-session state has no bound here.
Findings.Recommendation: Queue these reports with bounded concurrency or defer them to idle, and coalesce assessments that share the same session type/workspace scope while preserving the required per-session telemetry semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an existing Agents session and navigate among its main, side, or subagent chat tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session resolution/loading completes before the new assessment is launched; the assessment is fire-and-forget, so it is off the direct open/tab-render critical path but competes with subsequent UI work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover user and workspace prompt files for the agent, instructions, prompt, and skill types through `listPromptFiles`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four effective distinct prompt-type discoveries per cold assessment; repeated type requests coalesce only through the prompts-service cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat opens did not invoke migration assessment or prompt discovery from this lifecycle path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct UI critical path because the added call is detached, but it consumes I/O/CPU during and after navigation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Build an MCP support scope, wait for MCP initialization, iterate all known/installed servers, and resolve server configurations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scope assessment per distinct session-type/root key at a time, with per-server work; sequential chat opens recreate the disposed scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat-tab navigation did not acquire an MCP support scope for migration telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detached from rendering but creates background contention; cancellation of the navigation does not stop this MCP branch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue up to one aggregate telemetry event for each non-empty migration category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to four events per completed assessment, repeated on every chat open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No customization-migration telemetry was emitted from chat opens.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs after assessment and is off the direct navigation critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of chat-open actions in the same session, four migration categories, prompt-source size, and configured MCP-server count. Sequential tab opens are not deduplicated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Normally one assessment per click. A newer open cancels the prior navigation token, but the MCP branch does not consume that token; overlapping assessments for the same roots share a ref-counted scope, while sequential assessments recreate it after disposal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-file lists can be cached/coalesced per prompt type after locator event initialization; invalidation causes cold filesystem/provider discovery. MCP support is cached only for the lifetime of the acquired scope, which this assessment disposes on completion, so later tab opens rerun it. There is no report-once cache by session lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the UI callers, `_openChat` placement, full computation call chain, and short-lived MCP cache lifecycle are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact impact depends on tab-switch frequency, cold-cache state, prompt count, and MCP-server count; the repeated full assessment on every chat open is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work regression: chat-only navigation now reruns session-level migration assessment.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore persisted visible Agents sessions during workbench startup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The grid is restored before assessments are launched, so telemetry is not awaited by `restoreVisibleSessions`; however all assessments begin during `Workbench.restore` and contend with startup/early interaction work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold discovery of prompt files across user and workspace storage.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four effective prompt types globally when cache/coalescing is active; potentially repeated if caches are not initialized or have been invalidated.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session restore did not request migration prompt discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detached but runs during startup and contends with restore and extension activity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess known and installed MCP servers and resolve configuration for each distinct restored workspace scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: K concurrent scope assessments and O(K×M) per-server work after grouping identical session-type/root keys.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore performed session resolution/layout without MCP migration assessments.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by grid layout, but runs during startup and can delay responsiveness through CPU/async-resource contention.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create aggregate assessment telemetry for each non-empty category and restored session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration assessment telemetry was emitted during restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct restore path after each assessment completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N persisted visible sessions, reduced to K distinct session-type/root scope keys for concurrent MCP work, multiplied by M configured MCP servers per scope. The persisted visible-session collection is not bounded in this path.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The tight loop starts all N reports without awaiting or limiting them. Prompt discovery can coalesce globally by type; MCP work coalesces only for identical scope keys, so up to K distinct workspace assessments run concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm prompt caches avoid repeated file discovery. Cold prompt calls share cached promises when watcher initialization has enabled caching. MCP scopes for identical keys are shared only while overlapping and are removed when their final reference completes; distinct roots never coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: startup invocation, loop cardinality, detached scheduling, scope key, and per-server processing are directly visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: N and M vary by user, and identical roots reduce MCP concurrency, but the unbounded launch loop and per-distinct-workspace work are certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable startup concurrency burst; use bounded scheduling or scope-level coalescing.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or replace a draft in the Agents new-session composer
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The autorun launches assessment after a draft session becomes observable. It is not awaited by composer rendering or input, so it is off the direct interaction critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files required by the migration assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four effective prompt types for a cold draft assessment, generally shared through the prompts cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Draft observation did not run migration assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the composer critical path but may overlap workspace selection and provider startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess MCP support for the draft's session type and roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One per distinct draft scope, with per-MCP-server work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Draft changes did not acquire MCP assessment scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detached; old draft work is not canceled on replacement.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue aggregate telemetry for non-empty categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four events per draft assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration telemetry from this composer lifecycle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Usually one draft; additional assessments occur when workspace/session type changes, providers replace a draft, or background sends reseed the composer.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fire-and-forget with `CancellationToken.None`; replacement does not cancel prior work. Concurrent assessments with identical MCP scope keys share a scope, while different workspace roots do not.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt caches coalesce warm/cold type discovery as above. MCP scope results live only until all overlapping consumers release them. No draft-resource deduplication is present.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for execution and lack of cancellation; lower impact due to expected low frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Draft replacement is less frequent than chat navigation and typically has low cardinality, so no separate finding was warranted.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the assessment is intentionally tied to draft lifecycle and realistic multiplicity is usually small.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new empty chat in the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the editor model resolves and is attached, an empty model starts a detached assessment. The editor does not await it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt files for migration categories.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four effective prompt types per cold cache state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening an empty editor chat did not run this assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the editor-open critical path after model attachment.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess and resolve MCP server compatibility/configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scope per distinct session type/root set, with per-server work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration MCP assessment from editor new-chat open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Detached; canceled input suppresses telemetry but may not stop MCP work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to four events for the empty chat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration telemetry from this lifecycle.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One assessment per `setInput` of an empty chat, with cost proportional to prompt sources and MCP servers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The editor input token suppresses reporting after cancellation, but MCP computation itself does not consume the token. Overlapping identical scopes share an in-flight MCP assessment.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt discovery uses the shared per-type cache; MCP support is scope-lifetime cached and released after computation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for one assessment per empty editor input; insufficient evidence of harmful realistic repetition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repeated `setInput` for the same empty resource is possible but not established as a common hot path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: one detached assessment per editor-new-chat lifecycle is bounded under the established scenario.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 11 changed files. Reported two introduced regressions: repeated full assessment on every chat-tab open and unbounded concurrent assessment fan-out during startup restore. The telemetry aggregation itself is bounded to four categories; new-composer and editor-new-chat paths add detached work but lacked a sufficiently hot or scaling trigger for separate findings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
